ai-at-work.title: Meta launches Muse Code, an AI agent for large code bases
ai-at-work.excerpt: Meta expanded its AI coding offerings with a new agent that, it promises, can handle complex tasks with complex software.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Meta just released Muse Code, an AI agent designed to tackle the messy reality of large codebases instead of simple coding snippets. For digital workplace folks managing internal tools and custom platforms, this matters because your dev teams will start asking for access to it, and you'll need to figure out governance, security, and whether it actually works before letting it loose on production code. The real test isn't whether the AI can code, it's whether your organization can handle another tool that promises to save time but requires actual thinking about where it fits in your stack.

ai-at-work.title: Klaviyo acquires Elias Torres’ Agency in full-circle reunion for tech founders
ai-at-work.excerpt: The serial entrepreneur joins the e-commerce company as CPO to lead its AI agents.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Klaviyo bought Elias Torres' agency and he's now joining as Chief Product Officer to lead their AI agents division. This matters because it signals how seriously enterprise software companies are taking AI product development, and it shows they're willing to pay for proven builders rather than promote from within. After three decades watching tech cycles, I can tell you this setup usually works when the founder actually gets autonomy, but CPO roles at public companies have a way of becoming political minefields fast.

ai-at-work.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026’s Real World AI Stage features robots, automated factories, and extinct animals
ai-at-work.excerpt: On our new Real World AI stage, we’ll be focusing on the intersection between the digital and physical, and all the ways we’ll continue to see a blending of the two.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: TechCrunch is launching a "Real World AI" stage at Disrupt 2026 that will showcase how AI bridges digital and physical spaces, including robots, automated factories, and apparently extinct animals for some reason. This matters because digital workplace professionals need to understand how AI moves beyond chat interfaces and actually shows up in operations, supply chains, and physical infrastructure where real work happens. That said, if they're wheeling out robot dinosaurs to make their point about workplace automation, we've officially entered the territory where the conference itself has become the story instead of the actual insights.

ai-at-work.title: Anthropic is hiring an AI chip design team
ai-at-work.excerpt: Anthropic is building a team for designing its own custom AI chips. The Claude maker said it would co-design hardware and models to help its technology run faster and more efficiently.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Anthropic is building an in-house team to design custom AI chips rather than relying on off-the-shelf hardware from Nvidia and others. This matters because any organization betting heavily on AI infrastructure needs to understand that chip dependency is real and expensive, and vertical integration is becoming table stakes for serious players. Here's the thing though: everyone from OpenAI to Meta is doing this now, so Anthropic isn't being clever, just finally catching up like someone who joins the gym in March after New Year's resolutions.

tools-tech.title: I've dictated over 120,000 words with my voice - these are my 3 favorite tools (and one is free)
tools-tech.excerpt: I tested today's leading AI voice tools to find which delivers the best accuracy, privacy, corrections, and everyday productivity without slowing down real work.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Someone tested the major voice dictation tools and found three winners, including a free option that actually works. This matters because voice input is finally mature enough to be a real productivity lever, not just a novelty, which means your knowledge workers have legitimate alternatives to keyboard and mouse. The funny part is we've been promised "the future of voice" for twenty years, but it took AI to actually make it useful instead of frustrating.

tools-tech.title: Report: Passkey security issues could allow account takeover
tools-tech.excerpt: Given the widespread enterprise adoption of passkeys to replace passwords, a Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 report disclosing ways attackers are getting around passkey protections is concerning, analysts
tools-tech.dwp_take: Palo Alto Networks found that attackers can bypass passkey protections, but only after they've already broken into your system first. For digital workplace leaders rolling out passkeys as their password replacement strategy, this matters because it means passkeys alone won't save you if your broader security posture is weak. The real lesson here is that passkeys are great, but they're not a magic wand that lets you skip doing the actual security work.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft moves to limit AI use by its employees
tools-tech.excerpt: Until recently, it was common for companies and organizations to engage in “tokenmaxxing” — that is, maximizing their use of AI. But with AI costs going up, companies are now looking to save money, a
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft is telling its own employees to dial back their AI usage to control costs. This matters because if the company literally eating, sleeping, and breathing AI can't justify unlimited use, it signals that the AI gold rush economics don't actually work at scale. Turns out "tokenmaxxing" was just "spending money like it grows on trees" with extra steps.

tools-tech.title: Apple’s memory crisis is a big red flag for tech
tools-tech.excerpt: The memory crisis is getting worse for Apple, which is struggling to get enough memory chips together for its upcoming iPhone 18 Pro series smartphones. That’s according to tech journalist Tim Culpan.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Apple is facing a significant shortage of memory chips needed for its upcoming iPhone 18 Pro lineup, raising serious questions about their supply chain resilience. For digital workplace professionals managing enterprise device deployments, this signals potential delays and price increases that could impact corporate refresh cycles and mobility strategies. If a company with Apple's legendary supply chain muscle can't lock down enough memory chips, the rest of us should probably stop pretending our device roadmaps are anything more than educated guesses.

digital-culture.title: As employer burnout costs soar, EY gets at the heart of worker well-being with Vitality Index
digital-culture.excerpt: The tool is designed to help employers measure and boost workforce well-being.
digital-culture.dwp_take: EY launched the Vitality Index, a measurement tool aimed at helping employers track and improve workforce well-being as burnout costs climb. This matters because digital workplace leaders are increasingly expected to be stewards of employee health, not just productivity czars, and having actual data beats guessing at what's wrong. Here's the thing though: another dashboard measuring worker wellness doesn't fix the core problem, which is usually too much work, too few people, and not enough real flexibility to actually do the job without losing your mind.

digital-culture.title: Google’s Top AI Brains Are Leaving to Launch Discovery Loop
digital-culture.excerpt: Jeff Dean and other high-profile Google executives have founded Discovery Loop, a startup that will seek AI-powered breakthroughs in everything from drug discovery to chip design.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Google's top AI talent, including Jeff Dean, has left the company to start Discovery Loop, a new venture focused on using AI for breakthroughs in drug discovery, chip design, and similar fields. This matters to digital workplace pros because when your best people walk out the door to start their own thing, it signals either that your company culture has become unbearable or your innovation strategy isn't aggressive enough. After thirty years in this space, I've learned that losing Jeff Dean is like losing your star quarterback mid-season, except Google's the one paying his replacement's signing bonus through lost institutional knowledge.

industry-news.title: Google Pixel 11 Leak Reveals ‘HiLight’ Notification Feature, Raises Questions About Charging Claim
industry-news.excerpt: Leaked Google Pixel 11 marketing materials suggest a new HiLight notification feature, while a five-minute charging claim raises questions ahead of Google's launch. The post Google Pixel 11 Leak Revea
industry-news.dwp_take: Google's upcoming Pixel 11 appears to have a new HiLight notification system, though leaked marketing materials also mention a suspicious five-minute charging claim that's already drawing skepticism. For digital workplace folks, better notifications matter because they affect how employees stay focused and responsive throughout the workday. Honestly, if Google is claiming five-minute charging, I'd wait for the independent reviews before betting your device budget on it.

industry-news.title: Texas Pauses Data Center Grid Approvals as Power Requests Hit 474 GW
industry-news.excerpt: Texas paused grid approvals for new data centers as power requests hit 474 GW. Here’s what developers and IT leaders should expect. The post Texas Pauses Data Center Grid Approvals as Power Requests H
industry-news.dwp_take: Texas has hit pause on approving new data center connections to its power grid because demand has exploded to 474 gigawatts, far exceeding available capacity. For digital workplace pros, this matters because it affects where companies can actually build the infrastructure supporting remote work, cloud services, and collaboration tools that keep modern workforces running. Turns out you can't just keep stacking servers in Texas indefinitely, which is a shock to absolutely no one who understands basic physics.

industry-news.title: Apple Briefly Removes Telegram From App Store Over Reported CSAM Violation
industry-news.excerpt: Apple briefly removed Telegram from the App Store over reported CSAM, highlighting moderation failures and the distribution power held by app-store operators. The post Apple Briefly Removes Telegram F
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple pulled Telegram from its App Store due to child safety violations, then reinstated it after Telegram promised improvements. This matters because app stores function as gatekeepers for workplace communication tools, and when moderation fails at scale, it affects which platforms companies can safely deploy across their organizations. The real lesson here is that your enterprise messaging platform is only as trustworthy as the company running it and the store distributing it, which is why IT teams should stop assuming popular equals secure.

industry-news.title: Apple Plans iPhone-to-Windows Clipboard Support After Microsoft DMA Request
industry-news.excerpt: Apple plans an iOS framework for iPhone-to-Windows clipboard sharing after Microsoft’s EU request, but users face a wait until at least late 2027. The post Apple Plans iPhone-to-Windows Clipboard Supp
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple is finally going to let iPhones and Windows PCs share clipboard data, but not until late 2027 at the earliest, after Microsoft pushed the EU to make them do it. For digital workplace folks managing mixed-device environments, this is huge because copying text between an iPhone and a Windows machine has been absurdly painful for years. Still, if you're expecting this to suddenly make Apple and Windows play nicely together, I've got a bridge to sell you, because a single clipboard feature won't fix the deeper integration issues that plague hybrid workplaces.
